content: Pyridoxine deficiency, also known as vitamin B6 deficiency, is characterized by a range of clinical manifestations. These include a seborrheic dermatitis-like skin eruption, atrophic glossitis with ulceration, angular cheilitis, conjunctivitis, and intertrigo. Neurological symptoms such as excessive sleepiness (somnolence), confusion, and peripheral neuropathy are also commonly observed. Vitamin B6 plays a critical role as a co-factor for the enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase, which is responsible for converting glutamate, an excitatory neurotransmitter, into gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), an inhibitory neurotransmitter. In the context of vitamin B6 deficiency, there is an accumulation of glutamate and a reduction in GABA levels. This imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmitters can lead to seizures.
